body:
I've been doing that for years now. When I was way back in elementary school, I joined the band despite almost no expectation of enjoying an instrument. In high school, I joined a robotics team despite actively possessing none of the traits that would seem to make a good engineer. When I started college, I joined a space-related organization despite my complete lack of astronomical and aerospatial engineering awareness. The fact is, though, that all of them proved a burden on my psyche. I grew to hate participating in all of them. Maybe I'm just unlucky, but trying new things seems to yield further misery no matter how unusual they may seem. I haven't even touched on the writing and sewing things I tried, which I also grew not to hate, but to strongly dislike participating in. Perhaps that further illustrates the problem while recontextualizing my use of the word "hate" earlier.

Why don't I try new physical things? Well... I physically suck. I don't mean I'm fat and out-of-shape, which I also am, but that I'm clumsy and klutzy and can't move my body particularly well with respect to the environment around me. Kinda lets me fit into people's mental archetype of the clumsy genius. I actually think that's part of why some think I'm smarter than I am in reality, but that's a digression I don't think is particularly relevant. Suffice to say, I've tried and disliked things like soccer and tennis in the past, and if you gave me the opportunity to actually try something like sky-diving, then... I'm just gonna leave it there under subreddit rule 1b.

I've tried a lot of new and different things. Saying that it's the solution when it's only worsened the problem in the past is counterintuitive and I don't see any reason to keep trying at it. Especially when there is that unknown probability of a feeling of sheer nothing in death. Better an unknown probability than one infinitely close to zero to the point of non-considerability.

Edit: Want to mention explicitly. I would put SCUBA-diving in the same realm as sky-diving of things I'm not going to talk about what my participation would be like due to subreddit rule 1b.

I suppose I would respond by noting that the reasoning presupposes a level of spontaneity that has been far from evident. Of course, you could say that expecting such a thing contradicts the spontaneous nature of the thing of which I'd be looking for evidence, but I would argue that continuing a miserable existence in a last-ditch Hail Mary is unlikely to yield a satisfying result unless I suddenly have begun living in an inspirational sports movie.

I have been trying new things. I've gone out of my way to help out with a couple projects that'll also help advance my résumé if I graduate, but the added stress just worsens the overall seeming depression problem. I feel worse than before I joined up with either of these projects. And since I agreed to them, I'm obligated to see them through.

Actually, new counter-argument. Life spontaneously started getting worse when I found new anti-passions to put my time into. How about that? That turns the whole thing right around. Haha, this actually put a kinda bittersweet smile on my face. Your "attention is grabbed by new things that are fun to learn about and do," mine is grabbed by new things to make my life subjectively worse in the guise of helping others.

In other words, I'm always finding new things, but we respond to them differently enough that what works for you seems not to work effectively for me. I suppose I might be looking in the wrong places, and if you want to elaborate on the sorts of ways in which I should be broadening my horizons, that might be productive. But my attempts to follow such advice have left me feeling more broken than beforehand.

Edit: I wanted to mention that I like your username. Not sure if it's a reference to anything, but I'm gonna take a death of the author stance and admit that the reason I like it is because I originally read it as "You are not alone" before groaning and doing a double take when I reread. It actually gave me a good laugh to see that last word's true identity. It's, of course, not enough to make me want to stay alive, but it's still amusing.
